A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, and a table. All 10 pages of each were inspected; both end with references and contain no appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original quantitative evaluations on CMC and FMC, qualitative ablations, and a user study involving 40 participants in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original CMC/FMC evaluations, ablations, and 40-participant user study, including their reported outcomes.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the same text-reward optimization, sketch encoding, appearance encoding, sequential integration, and losses. Renaming Subjective Camera 0.1 to 1.0 introduces no procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same composed multi-concept sketches in CMC, freehand scenes in FMC, and participant-provided memory readouts. No dataset, task, population, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 5 retain ControlNet, T2I-Adapter, Uni-ControlNet, Multi-Sketch, PNP, and FreeControl. The user study retains FreeControl, text-reward optimization, and text-reward optimization with overall sketch guidance as comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain 142 CMC scenes, 42 FMC sketches, the same FID/CLIP-T/HPS/CLIP-I metrics, and identical implementation settings. The 12-plus-28 participant design, four questions, two-minute readout period, and reference-viewing controls are unchanged.

E4.justification: The sketch-optimization comparison in Figure 4, component ablations in Figure 6, and participant-group/reference-viewing controls in Figure 8 are identical. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain the same user-preference reporting and significance statements in Section 4.4. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or additional statistical procedures.

E6.justification: All Table 1 values and qualitative results match, as do the preference percentages in Figures 7–8. For example, the proposed method retains CMC FID 11.56, FMC FID 10.18, and FMC CLIP-I 0.797.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and all 13 numbered equations are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about training-free sequential reconstruction, benchmark performance, and user preference. The 0.1-to-1.0 name update does not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of concept interference and preference results, including the image-quality exception. Limitations concerning small sketches, imperfect scene reconstruction, and sensitivity to sketch order and quality are unchanged.

D1.justification: The disclosed learning rate, thresholds, loss weights, RTX 4090 hardware, and 512×512 input resolution remain identical. The project-page address and its hyperlink target are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning passages, and all 38 numbered references are unchanged. No cited work or relationship to prior research is added, removed, or revised.

P1.justification: Subjective Camera 0.1 becomes Subjective Camera 1.0 in the title, abstract, and final paragraph; the arXiv version/date stamp also changes. The remaining wording and section organization are unchanged apart from extraction spacing.

P2.justification: Visual inspection confirms that Figures 1–8 and Table 1 retain the same content, captions, structure, and placement. The page layout and section breaks remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 changes the system name and version/date stamp while retaining the same method, evidence, explanations, limitations, and presentation. These editorial updates establish no meaningful improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
